comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C36, C37, C49, C146. Both support the negative results for lin-4 and the positive results for glp-1 mutants. OpenEval notes these are unpublished observations ('data not shown'), slightly weakening reproducibility, but peer reviewers accepted without concern.

Perfect agreement on claims C99, C100, C101. Both support the distinction between lin-29a-specific and null phenotypes and the WormTracker morphological analysis. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on claims C109, C110, C111, C112. Both support the automated behavioral phenotyping and circuit-specific rescue experiments. OpenEval provides more detail on sample sizes (n=20) and specificity of effects.

Strong agreement on claims C88, C89, C90, C92, C96, C97, C98 regarding broad roles of lin-29a. Both evaluations support the findings. Peer review noted only minor figure labeling issues, not data quality concerns.

Strong agreement on claims C62, C63, C65, C66, C67, C68 regarding expression patterns and temporal control. Both support the use of multiple reporter types and appropriate controls. No concerns raised by peer reviewers.

Strong agreement on claims C121, C123-C129, C131, C133, C134 regarding mab-3 and dmd-3 regulation. Both support the extension of the intersectional control model to additional targets. Peer review noted only a minor text reference error.
Strong agreement on claims C102, C103, C105, C107 regarding behavioral phenotypes and rescue. Both support the findings with adequate sample sizes. No concerns raised by peer reviewers.

Strong agreement on claims C83, C84, C85, C86, C87 regarding lin-29a sufficiency experiments. Both support the cell autonomy, temporal sufficiency, and sex-specificity override demonstrations. Peer reviewers were very enthusiastic.

Agreement on claims C59, C61 regarding mab-10 null allele showing normal differentiation. Both support this negative result defining pathway specificity. OpenEval raises questions about whether xe44 is a true null, but peer reviewers accepted without concern.

Agreement on claims C1, C22-C27, C38-C42 regarding heterochronic pathway control of AIM differentiation. Both strongly support the genetic evidence. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of opposing phenotypes and quantification, while peer reviewers were very enthusiastic about conceptual and technical aspects.

Agreement on claim C158 being speculative. Both evaluations mark this as uncertain/untested. OpenEval notes it requires 'further biochemical studies,' while peer reviewer 1 suggested testing UNC-3 binding sites but would not delay publication.

Partial overlap on claims C113, C114, C118 regarding intersectional control. Both support the sex-determination pathway control and the intersectional model. OpenEval also covers C115-C117 (terminal selectors), which peer review addresses separately in R9.

Partial overlap on claims C53, C54, C55 regarding differential lin-29 requirements in AIM vs CEM neurons. Both support these findings. OpenEval also covers C82, C87 regarding lin-29a-specific alleles, which peer review addresses in R5.

Partial overlap on claims C79, C80, C81 regarding genetic epistasis and direct repression. Both support the findings. OpenEval focuses on epistasis experiments, while peer review R4 also covers expression patterns (C71-C73, C76) addressed by OpenEval R6.

Partial overlap on claims C115, C116, C117 regarding terminal selector requirements. Both support the cell-type-specific control. OpenEval also covers C157, while peer review R9 also addresses sex-determination pathway (C4, C113, C114, C118).

Partial overlap on claims C71, C72, C73, C76 regarding lin-29a expression patterns. Both support the findings. OpenEval R6 focuses on expression analysis, while peer review R4 also covers epistasis (C79-C81) addressed by OpenEval R7.

Partial overlap on claims C31-C34, C45-C48 regarding CEM differentiation timing. Both support the heterochronic pathway control. OpenEval R1 covers broader genetic manipulations, while peer review R3 specifically addresses CEM neurons.

Minimal overlap on claims C28, C29, C30. Both support these findings. OpenEval R1 groups these with broader heterochronic pathway evidence, while peer review R2 focuses on differential requirements across neuron types.
